transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Uh, yeah… I guess I came in because my eating’s gotten kind of out of hand after work. I do late shifts, and sometimes I’ll stop for food on the way home, and then when I get back I just keep eating—like the takeout meal, then chips, sweets, whatever’s around the apartment.

It’s weird because I’ll be thinking I’m just unwinding after work, you know, and then suddenly I look at all the wrappers or containers and I’m kind of shocked by how much I actually ate.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Yeah… sometimes. Not laxatives, really, and I wouldn’t say I’m doing some huge workout thing, but… after I get home and I’ve eaten way too much takeout or snacks, I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s like I get this panic that it’s just sitting in me and it’s going to turn into weight. I know that sounds bad. I don’t even always plan it—like I’ll be putting the containers in the trash and then I’m just thinking about it, and… yeah, sometimes I do it.
How often do you find yourself making yourself vomit after these eating episodes, and does it happen every time you overeat or only sometimes?

It’s not every single time I overeat. I mean, sometimes I just feel awful and kind of sit with it, or I fall asleep, especially after a late shift. But other times, yeah… if I get home and I’ve had too much takeout or snacks, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s usually when I get that panicky feeling, like it’s just sitting in me and it’s going to turn into weight. I don’t have an exact count, but it happens sometimes after those episodes, not every time.

latest_inference.note: The patient reported inducing vomiting after eating episodes, which occurs frequently enough to suggest Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) rather than Binge-Eating Disorder (F50.81). This behavior, although not occurring every time, aligns more strongly with Bulimia Nervosa.
